name: Kaluki (European)
description: Kaluki (also spelled Kalooki) is a widely played European variant of Rummy, characterized by its use of two 52-card decks plus Jokers. Primarily played for points over multiple hands, it features a 51-point initial meld threshold and a distinctive 'Joker Exchange' rule where players can 'rescue' wild cards from the board.

overview.description: Kaluki (also spelled Kalooki) is a widely played European variant of Rummy, characterized by its use of two 52-card decks plus Jokers. Primarily played for points over multiple hands, it features a 51-point initial meld threshold and a distinctive 'Joker Exchange' rule where players can 'rescue' wild cards from the board.

history.origins: Believed to be a mid-20th century evolution of earlier Rummy games like Rummikub (the tile version) and standard 500 Rummy. The name likely derives from the Hungarian or Eastern European 'Kalooki' variants.
timeline: 1940s: Rummy variants using two decks emerge in the US and Europe.
1960s: Standardized rules for 'Kalooki 51' appear in Western card books.
2000s: Online gaming platforms bring Kaluki to a global audience.
Present: A staple social game, often associated with bridge clubs and retirement social circles.
history.cultural: In North America, it is often called 'Double-Deck Rummy' or simply 'Kalooki'. It is known for being a 'polite' but intensely competitive game.
history.evolution: The game branched into a 'Contract' version (popular in the Caribbean) and a 'Point' version (popular in Europe), with the latter focusing on a single high opening score.

setup.deck: 106 cards. Two standard 52-card decks plus 2 Jokers. Suits are Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 cards dealt singly. The next card is turned face-up to start the discard pile; remaining cards form the stock.
setup.equipment: Standard cards, score sheet, chips or counters for stakes (optional).

rules.objective: Empty your hand by forming melds on the table and have the lowest total points at the end of the session.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Drawing**: Each turn, draw either the top card of the stock or the top discard. 2. **Melding**: If you can form valid melds meeting the initial point requirement (51 points), lay them face-up. 3. **Building**: After initial meld, add cards to any existing meld (yours or opponents'). 4. **Discarding**: End turn by discarding one card face-up.
keyRules: Initial meld must total at least 51 points (house rule may vary to 40)
Sets: 3-4 cards of same rank, all different suits (no duplicates)
Runs: 3+ consecutive cards of same suit; Aces are high only (A-K-Q valid, 3-2-A invalid)
Jokers are wild and can substitute any card in a meld
Jokers in hand at end of play count as 15 penalty points
Building: After initial meld, add cards to extend existing melds on table
Joker Exchange: A melded Joker can be 'stolen' by replacing it with the natural card it represents

strategy.basic: Prioritize reaching the initial meld threshold (51 points) as quickly as possible. Use high-value cards (Aces, Face cards) to meet this requirement efficiently.
strategy.intermediate: Joker Management: Hold Jokers until you can use them in a meldâ€”15 penalty points is severe. Watch for opportunities to exchange for Jokers on the table. Track which cards have been discarded to calculate drawing odds.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Discarding: Avoid discarding cards that could help opponents complete their initial meld or extend their existing melds. The 'Late Meld' strategy: Hold back small melds to prevent opponents from building on them.
tips: Three Aces = 33 pointsâ€”more than half the 51-point requirement
Don't hold Jokers too longâ€”the 15-point penalty can eliminate you
Watch opponent discards to deduce what suits they are collecting
In sets with Jokers, you need both missing suits to exchangeâ€”plan accordingly

scoring.description: Winner of a round scores 0. Losers score points for cards left in hand.
scoring.winCondition: Game continues until all but one player have been eliminated by exceeding 150 penalty points. The last surviving player wins the pool.

synthesis.shortDescription: A sophisticated two-deck rummy where strategy meets calculation. Build your 51-point opening, wield your Jokers wisely, and outmaneuver opponents in this classic European favorite.
